native_result.query: In which century did the Diversity in Pottery Form collapses and Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneuosly?
native_result.HypoA: Around 1800 BCE, Diversity in Pottery Form collapses, while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases.
native_result.HypoB: The Diversity in Pottery Form collapses and the Diversity in Pottery Decoration simultaneously increases in the 18th century BCE — the century labeled 1700 BCE (1800–1701 BCE convention). In that single century the PotteryForm z-score plunges from +0.74 to −1.13 (Δ = −1.87, z = −3.38, the largest one-century decline in the entire 4100–500 BCE record) while PotteryDecoration jumps in the same century from −0.48 to +0.97 (Δ = +1.45, z = +3.18), then continues to its maximum plateau of +1.53 by 1000 BCE, while Form remains locked at its series minimum of −1.13 through 500 BCE. 1700 BCE is the only century in the record where a strong Form decline (z ≤ −1) coincides with a strong Decoration rise (z ≥ +1); the only other Form-decline century (2800 BCE) shows Decoration falling as well.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded time_series_data.csv (3,601 annual rows, CE −4100..−500, CE negative = BCE) and extracted the century-mark z-series for PotteryForm/PotteryDecoration (raw columns hold exactly 37 values at the 100-year marks CE −4100..−500; the annual _inter columns are linear interpolations verified numerically identical at the century marks). 2) Computed one-century changes and z-scored them across the series. 3) Defined collapse = Form decline event (z-scored change ≤ −1) and increase = Decoration rise event (z-scored change ≥ +1); a purely level-based collapse flag was rejected because it mislabels the post-collapse plateau (1600–500 BCE, Form constant at −1.13) as collapse. 4) Required coincidence of both events within the same century bin → unique century: 1700 BCE. 5) Cross-checked against (a) the annual PotteryForm_inter/PotteryDecoration_inter series (the step falls entirely within the 1700 BCE century) and (b) capital.csv ZKeform/Zkeverz (BCE labels verified to align with time_series_data CE = −BCE; BCE 1700 row identical). Data-quality flags: capital.csv rows BCE 4300/4200 duplicate the CE −500 values and lie outside the time-series range (excluded, non-driving); the pollen openness record (CE −4785..−702, Belau/Woserin PC1 with interpolated and 50–250-year smoothed variants) fully covers the pottery window and is treated as supporting context only.
